Measure first.

- Run `pytest --durations=10` to list the 10 slowest tests.
- Run `jest --runTestsByPath --coverage=false` to isolate slow Jest files.
- Run `go test -cpuprofile cpu.out ./...` to profile Go tests.
- Run `pytest --collect-only -q` to count collected tests.
- Run `pytest -x --lf` to rerun only failed tests.

Parallelize execution.

- Run `pytest -n auto` with `pytest-xdist`.
- Run `jest --maxWorkers=4` to cap worker count.
- Run `go test -parallel 8 ./...` for Go tests.
- Run `cargo test --test-threads=4` for Rust tests.
- Run `python manage.py test --parallel=4` for Django tests.

Cut I/O.

- Replace real databases with `sqlite:///:memory:` for unit tests.
- Use `pytest-django --reuse-db` to avoid recreating the test database.
- Use `pytest-django --nomigrations` when schema changes are not under test.
- Use `unittest.mock.patch("requests.get")` to block network calls.
- Use `tmp_path` instead of global temp directories.
- Replace `time.sleep(1)` with `freezegun.freeze_time("2024-01-01")`.

Reduce setup cost.

- Move expensive setup to `@pytest.fixture(scope="session")`.
- Cache dependencies in `~/.cache/pip` and `node_modules`.
- Run local tests with `--no-coverage`.
- Run `jest --no-cache` only when cache corruption is suspected.
- Use `--tb=no --quiet` to reduce terminal output overhead.

Fix test design.

- Convert slow end-to-end tests into unit tests using `FakeRepository`.
- Split monolithic tests into `test_create_user` and `test_update_user`.
- Use `@pytest.mark.parametrize("input,expected", [...])` to avoid duplicated setup.
- Use `--maxfail=1` to stop after the first failure.
- Use `--timeout=5` with `pytest-timeout` to kill hanging tests.

Tune CI.

- Cache `~/.cache/pip`, `node_modules`, and `.pytest_cache`.
- Run `pytest --lf` on changed files only.
- Run `vitest --changed` to test only changed files.
- Run `go test ./pkg/...` instead of `./...` when only one package changed.
- Set `--failfast` for Python test runners.

results.out:
Use this release process:

- Cut a release branch: `git checkout -b release/1.2.0` from `main`.
- Freeze scope: update `CHANGELOG.md` with `## [1.2.0] - YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Bump version: set `1.2.0` in `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, or `Cargo.toml`.
- Run CI: execute `npm test`, `pytest`, `cargo test`, or `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- Build artifacts: run `npm run build`, `docker build -t app:1.2.0 .`, or `make dist`.
- Tag the release: `git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Release 1.2.0"`.
- Publish artifacts: run `npm publish --access public`, `docker push app:1.2.0`, or upload to the artifact registry.
- Deploy to staging: run `kubectl set image deployment/app app=app:1.2.0 -n staging`.
- Smoke test staging: run `curl -fsS https://staging.example.com/healthz`.
- Promote to production: run `kubectl set image deployment/app app=app:1.2.0 -n production`.
- Verify production: confirm `GET /healthz` returns `200` and `GET /version` returns `1.2.0`.
- Roll back if needed: redeploy `app:1.1.9` or run `git revert <bad-commit-sha>`.
